item.title: UK prime minister calls actions of Russian warship reckless but not sinister
item.description: UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer says the crew of a Russian warship of acted recklessly in firing a warning shots near a British yacht in the English Channel

item.title: Sudan’s young women return to international soccer as war and taboos linger
item.description: Sudan's under-17 women's national soccer team has made its first international appearance since civil war erupted in the country

item.title: UK military investigates after Russian warship fires warning shots near yacht in the Channel
item.description: A Russian warship has fired warning shots near a U.K.-registered pleasure yacht in the English Channel

item.title: Mideast oil producers step up plans to bypass the Strait of Hormuz
item.description: Before the war in Iran, roughly 15 million barrels of Persian Gulf oil were shipped each day through the Strait of Hormuz

item.title: ICC drops war crimes case against fugitive Sudan rebel Abdallah Banda
item.description: International Criminal Court judges have reluctantly dropped the case against a Sudanese rebel accused of attacking peacekeepers in Darfur nearly 20 years ago

item.title: Pakistan rejects Amnesty call for war crimes probe into Kabul airstrike
item.description: Pakistan has rejected Amnesty International’s call for an investigation into a March airstrike on a drug rehabilitation center in the Afghan capital that the rights group said could amount to a war crime, dismissing the allegations as unsupported

item.title: Russia's biggest online retailer is the latest target of Ukraine's attacks
item.description: Ukrainian attacks on Russian warehouses have targeted Wildberries, Russia's largest online retailer
